_readme: The title screen, driven by real keys.
It cannot prove Continue against a real save, and the reason is worth writing down: a
--qa-script run points saves at user://qa_saves and empties it at BOOT, so a session can
never start with one. The with-a-save branch is asserted in tests/integration/test_title.gd,
which can write a slot and rebuild the title inside one process.
What this proves is the part only real keys can: that the refusal is a refusal, that one
press starts a run, and that a save written after a title boot is a save like any other.

steps.text: the title, through the real input map. Continue is refused with nothing saved, and the cursor knows it - it opens on New game rather than on a row a press would bounce off. Rows: Continue, New game, Credits - and this session never goes below New game, so the row M43 appended moved nothing here.

up onto Continue and press it: the screen is still here afterwards, which is the refusal. Asserted rather than assumed - a Continue that quietly did nothing and one that quietly loaded nothing look identical from outside.
back down onto New game, and the run begins
save standing here, so the title has something to offer next time. Rows: Resume, Items, Equipment, Status, Save, Load, Sound - so Save is four move_downs.
out of the menu, and back to the title the long way round - through the game-over screen's Title row, which is the only route back that does not need a death
